item.title: Chinese premier urges China, ASEAN to stand united, overcome distractions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
MANILA, Nov. 16 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Monday that in a turbulent and complex world, China and ASEAN should stand united, overcome distractions and work together to build a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. Li made the remarks during the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila. As this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that over the past five years, the world has witnessed a growing trend of unilateralism and protectionism, while geopolitical conflicts have flared up one after another. Against this backdrop, China-ASEAN cooperation has forged ahead, achieving both quantitative growth and qualitative improvements, with cooperation mechanisms further consolidated and connectivity steadily enhanced, he said. The extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons, Li said. He stressed that both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development. These experiences and lessons are a valuable asset shared by both sides and should be upheld and put to full use over the long term, Li said. Five years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed that China and ASEAN work together to build a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home, Li said, adding that both China and ASEAN countries cherish the culture of family and are geographically close and bound by strong people-to-people ties. The profound bonds forged over generations should not, and will not, be affected by temporary events or circumstances, he said. Li urged China and ASEAN countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village. He called on the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. China looks forward to the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea, which will provide a solid institutional guarantee for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea, Li said. He also called for promoting regional development and prosperity, stressing the need for both sides to take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity," in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules. The premier said China applauds the establishment of a China-ASEAN mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with ASEAN to successfully hold the China-ASEAN Year of artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation next year, advance "AI+" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development. Li also called for improving the well-being of the people, voicing China's readiness to continue to contribute to the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund and strengthen cooperation with ASEAN in areas including poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation, food security, maternal and child health, so as to promote sustainable development in the region. Commending the fruitful outcomes achieved over the five years since the establishment of the ASEAN-China comprehensive strategic partnership, leaders of ASEAN countries expressed readiness to strengthen strategic communication and political mutual trust with China, fully implement the ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and deepen cooperation in areas including economy and trade, connectivity, AI, clean energy, digital economy and combating transnational crime. They thanked China for its consistent support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture and its commitment to the peaceful settlement of disputes. They also expressed the hope for an early conclusion of the COC in the South China Sea, jointly safeguarding regional peace and stability, and building an ASEAN-China community with a shared future. It was announced during the meeting that the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will enter into force on Dec. 1, 2026, and 2027 has been designated as the Year of AI cooperation. Outcome documents were released, covering the 5th anniversary of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, energy partnership building, and deeper forestry cooperation.

item.title: Chinese premier returns to Beijing after attending China-ASEAN Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang returned to Beijing on Monday after attending the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Philippines. When leaving Manila, Li was seen off at the airport by Philippine Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Chinese Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan and Chinese Ambassador to ASEAN Wang Qing.

item.title: Xi congratulates Jinan University on its 120th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday sent a congratulatory letter to Jinan University, celebrating its 120th founding anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, extended congratulations to the faculty, students and alumni of the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward its patriotic traditions and distinctive educational features, and to foster more young talent among compatriots in Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan and overseas Chinese. He also called on the university to carry forward and promote Chinese culture and advance friendly exchanges between China and the world. The university was asked to improve its education and teaching quality and make new contributions to pooling strength among overseas Chinese and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1906, the university in south China's Guangdong Province has, over the past 120 years, nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, as well as for more than 170 countries.

item.title: Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area Updated: November 16, 2026 18:37Xinhua ZHONGSHAN, Guangdong, Nov. 16 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary. Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of this mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries. Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan would seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a sound business environment, and vigorously promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. On the new journey, it is necessary to emulate, inherit and promote his invaluable spirit, and inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Xi said. During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) off to a good start.

item.title: China, U.S. hold first meeting of trade council under economic, trade consultation mechanism
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
BEIJING, Nov. 14 -- China and the United States held the first meeting of the trade council under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Friday, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday. Guided by the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, the meeting focused on implementing the outcomes of previous rounds of bilateral economic and trade consultations. The two sides had a candid, in-depth and constructive exchange on tariffs, the reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement covering about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of each other's goods, agricultural trade and other issues of mutual concern. Both sides will continue to strengthen communication through the trade council, work to resolve their respective economic and trade concerns, further expand cooperation and shorten the list of issues, so as to help build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, the ministry noted. In May 2026, China and the United States agreed to establish a trade council to address their respective concerns in trade cooperation. The two sides held the eighth round of their economic and trade consultations in New York and Washington, D.C. from Sept. 20 to 23. During the consultations, they agreed to reduce tariffs on about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of goods imported from each other on a reciprocal basis, with tariffs on around 90 percent of the covered products to be lowered to most-favored-nation rates.

item.title: China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth Updated: November 12, 2026 10:38Xinhua BEIJING, Nov. 12 -- China on Thursday held a gathering in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addressed the gathering. Also present at the event were Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. More than a century ago, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. He died in 1925.

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses.

item.title: Chinese premier signs decree to revise, repeal certain administrative regulations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 -- A decision by China's State Council to amend and repeal certain administrative regulations was made public on Thursday. Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating the decision, which aims to address pointless formalities to lighten the burden on those working on the ground, implement the reform of Party and state institutions, and ensure the consistency of relevant laws and regulations. Certain provisions of 14 administrative regulations were revised, and four regulations were repealed, according to the document. The State Council decided to revise a regulation on river course administration to align it with related provisions in the country's Ecological and Environmental Code. Meanwhile, a regulation on the limits of liability for maritime passenger transport between Chinese ports was repealed to better meet the needs of ongoing reform and development, and address practical realities in relevant areas. The decision takes effect on the date of its promulgation.
